title: A session started in the same second as a password reset survives it for up to an hour (and one from the second of a disable comes back on re-enable)
label: bug
role: founder resetting any member; any member changing own password
steps:
1. Sign in as a member at the start of a wall-clock second (POST /api/local/session).
2. In the same second, the founder sets a new password (POST /api/founder/users/{id}/password).
3. Call GET /api/platform/org with the old access token.
4. Control: sign in, wait 1.2 s, reset, call again.
5. Disable the account and re-enable it within the same second as a sign-in, then reuse that token.
expected: Every access token made before the reset (or the disable) is refused at once (401 session_ended). The plan (Part 2.8) and platform.py's own docstring say 'a password change or a disable ... refuses older tokens at once'.
actual: 3 of 3 same-second trials: the old access token answers 200 after the reset; only its refresh token is revoked (401). The control (1.2 s gap) gives 401. A token from the second of a disable answers 401 while disabled but 200 again after re-enable. Cause: sessions_from is int(time) and the check is `iat < sessions_from` (platform.py:342, :354, :365), so a token with iat equal to that second passes. An attacker who knows a password and signs in every ~150 ms (one PBKDF2 each) almost always holds a token minted in the reset's second, and keeps an hour of access after the owner resets the password. The same code is in solarlytics-backend platform.py:342/354/365.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f64857cc-0ca7-5cbb-b665-d2b474fb2fb8/scratchpad/audit/supa-auth/t4.out: '0 same second sign-in done 0.16s, reset done 0.23s old access -> 200 old refresh -> 401' (x3); 'control sign-in 1.2 s before reset old access -> 401'; 'disable same second while disabled -> 401 after re-enable -> 200'. Code: backend/gridlytics/platform.py:342 `iat < found["sessions_from"]`, :354 `int(_clock())`; identity.issue_local iat in whole seconds (identity.py:199). Fix: compare against a session id (the refresh family, revoked on reset) or a millisecond stamp, or set sessions_from to now+1 and issue the replacement session's token with iat >= it. Add a regression test that signs in and resets within one second.

title: 'Forgotten your password? Ask your company's administrator' sends people to someone who cannot reset a password, clear a lockout or change a name or email
label: spec-mismatch
role: any member; owner/admin of a company
steps:
1. Open /login and read the hint under Sign in.
2. As a company owner (app role admin), open /settings > Members: there is no 'set password', 'one-time password' or 'clear lockout' action.
3. PUT /api/users/{member} with {"password":...}, {"name":...} or {"email":...}.
4. POST /api/users/{id}/password.
expected: Under Solarlytics' model, only the founder (OnyxLeaf) issues and resets passwords, and its login page says 'Forgotten your password? Ask us for a new one' (solarlytics-frontend pages/auth/Login.tsx:69). Or, per the Gridlytics plan (EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md line 736), the company admin issues a one-time password with a forced change and can clear a lockout, and the hint names the admin. Either the words or the feature must hold.
actual: The hint names the company administrator (login-page.tsx:71), but an admin has no path. PUT /api/users refuses password, name and email with 'The name, the email address and the password are kept by the sign-in service: change them in My account' (api.py:476). My account changes only the caller's own password, so another member's name or email can be changed nowhere; the email cannot be changed even by the founder (PATCH /api/founder/users accepts only disabled and name). POST /api/users/{id}/password gives 404. A person locked out or with a forgotten password has no route except an unstated email to OnyxLeaf.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f64857cc-0ca7-5cbb-b665-d2b474fb2fb8/scratchpad/audit/supa-auth/t6.out (owner of AUDIT Tenancy A): PUT ['name'] / ['password'] / ['email'] -> 422 'kept by the sign-in service: change them in My account'; POST /api/users/{id}/password -> 404. Files: gridlytics-frontend/frontend/src/features/auth/login-page.tsx:71; gridlytics-frontend/frontend/src/features/org/account-page.tsx (read-only name and email); backend/gridlytics/api.py:476; backend/gridlytics/routes_founder.py:329-333. Work: either restore Solarlytics' 'Ask us' wording and say in Members that OnyxLeaf adds people and resets passwords, or build plan line 736: POST /api/users/{id}/password (manage_users, one-time, must_change flag), a lockout clear, and an audit row.

title: No supabase/ folder: Solarlytics' SQL (preflight, migration, rollback) and its owner checklist were never ported, though the code and plan reference them
label: feature-gap
steps:
1. ls gridlytics-backend: there is no supabase/ folder and no *.sql file anywhere, nor in git history (`git log --all -- supabase` is empty).
2. Compare solarlytics-backend/supabase/{README.md, sql/solar_000_preflight.sql, migrations/solar_001_accounts_and_companies.sql, migrations/solar_001_rollback.sql}.
3. Read store_founder.py:8 and api.py's docstrings, which point at supabase/migrations.
actual:
Nothing was ported, and DESIGN_LOG's lift section (lines 244-257) does not record dropping it.

The lifted code expects the schema anyway:
- companies._project_context calls rpc/get_my_context;
- store_founder._Project writes `companies` and `company_memberships` through PostgREST with the service-role key.

So GRIDLYTICS_AUTH_MODE=supabase would meet a project with no matching tables or functions. None of Boxlytics' Google, sign-up, invites or onboarding should come with it; the owner's rule matches Solarlytics' checklist exactly.
evidence: `find gridlytics-backend -name '*.sql'` gives nothing; backend/gridlytics/store_founder.py:7-8 ('PostgREST for its `companies` and `company_memberships` (supabase/migrations)'); companies.py:115-216 (the supabase-mode context); plan .scratch/plan/docs/plan/build-plan/EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md:789; research/U2-backends.md:90, 125 (test_supabase_sql.py, 484 lines), 338; solarlytics-backend/supabase/README.md sections 2-9.

title: Supabase mode is half-lifted: the backend carries it, but the web app is local-only, so GRIDLYTICS_AUTH_MODE=supabase leaves no way to sign in
label: spec-mismatch
steps:
1. Read frontend/src/app/env.ts:9: VITE_AUTH_MODE is z.enum(['local']).
2. grep the web app for supabase: no client, no auth service, no /reset-password route.
3. Read frontend/src/test/source-rules.test.ts:35-37, which fails any file importing @supabase/.
4. Read backend api.py:530: in supabase mode routes_local is not mounted, so /api/local/session does not exist.
actual:
Only the backend half exists:
- identity.py, companies.py and store_founder.py are identical to Solarlytics, including JWKS verification and the Admin API.
- The web app can only post /api/local/session, which a supabase-mode backend does not mount, so every sign-in fails.
- .env.example says 'Only "local" ... is built today'.

Neither DESIGN_LOG nor HANDOFF section 8 lists this as a deviation or as open work. PLT-11 ('Supabase sign-in mode live', later) covers making a project live, not omitting the carried mode.
evidence: gridlytics-frontend/frontend/src/app/env.ts:9; gridlytics-frontend/.env.example ('Only "local" ... is built today'); gridlytics-frontend/frontend/src/test/source-rules.test.ts:35-37; backend/gridlytics/api.py:530; solarlytics-frontend/frontend/src/services/supabase.client.ts, services/auth.service.ts, pages/auth/ResetPassword.tsx, main.tsx:58, .env.example; solarlytics-frontend/frontend/tests/supabaseauth.test.ts.

title: Members list drops Solarlytics' supabase branch: in supabase mode nobody who has not signed in yet is listed, so an admin cannot set a role ahead
label: bug
steps:
1. Read backend/gridlytics/api.py:426-436: `_not_seen()` reads only platformdb.company_members (the local registry).
2. Compare solarlytics-backend api.py `_not_seen(request)`. In supabase mode it asks rpc/company_list_members with the caller's own token, for an owner or admin only (`_project_members`, with a 1 MB cap and a fallback to people seen).
expected: In supabase mode the project's memberships are listed, as Solarlytics does. That is what lets an admin give a role before a member's first sign-in, and it is covered by solarlytics test_members_b4b.py:369-470.
actual: In supabase mode platform.db holds no memberships (the founder console writes them to the project), so `_not_seen()` returns [] and PUT /api/users/{id} for a person not seen yet answers 404 'No such user'. Neither `_project_members` nor its tests were carried, and DESIGN_LOG does not mention it.
evidence: backend/gridlytics/api.py:426-429 (`_not_seen()` reads platformdb.company_members); `grep -rn '_project_members\|company_list_members' backend/` finds nothing; solarlytics-backend/backend/solarlytics/api.py:4935-4990; solarlytics-backend/backend/tests/test_members_b4b.py:369-470.

title: Backend .gitignore does not ignore .env files, so a root .env holding the service-role key or founder secrets would be committed
label: bug
steps:
1. Run `cat gridlytics-backend/.gitignore`.
2. Run `git check-ignore -v .env .env.founder .env.production` in gridlytics-backend.
expected: As in solarlytics-backend, solarlytics-frontend and gridlytics-frontend: `.env`, `.env.*` and `!.env*.example` (U2 line 270).
actual: The ignore list is data/, .scratch/, caches, demo/DEMO_ACCOUNTS.local.md, release/ and *.egg-info only. git check-ignore reports nothing for .env, .env.founder or .env.production, so a deployer's .env with GRIDLYTICS_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY or GRIDLYTICS_FOUNDER_* would be staged by `git add -A`.
evidence: gridlytics-backend/.gitignore (8 lines); `git check-ignore -v .env .env.founder .env.production` prints nothing. Compare solarlytics-backend/.gitignore:7-9 and gridlytics-frontend/.gitignore:4-6.

title: Sign-in throttling is about 200 times looser than Supabase's defaults: 1,200 tries a minute per address, about 50 ms of PBKDF2 each, no per-account cap across addresses
label: bug
steps:
1. Send 25 sequential sign-ins with random unknown emails.
2. Send 40 more, 20 at a time.
3. Read auth.RATE_LIMITS and routes_local.local_session.
expected: Throttling comparable to the Supabase Auth mode the owner may switch to: about 30 sign-in requests per 5 minutes per IP by default [recalled]. Also a cap per account across addresses, so the lock cannot be stepped around, and an unauthenticated flood that cannot buy unbounded hashing.
actual:
All 65 attempts got 401, none 429. Sequential: 52 ms median each. Concurrent: 0.86 s median and 1.55 s max latency, so the single API process saturates.
- RATE_PUBLIC is 1,200 a minute per address (auth.py:79-80).
- Unknown-email tries are not recorded.
- The lock is per (email, address) only (platform.lock_wait), so one address can try 4 passwords per account per 15 minutes across every account, and many addresses are unlimited per account.
- PBKDF2 runs 200,000 rounds (auth.py:52), below OWASP's 600,000 for PBKDF2-SHA256 [recalled].
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f64857cc-0ca7-5cbb-b665-d2b474fb2fb8/scratchpad/audit/supa-auth/t5.out: 'sequential unknown-email sign-ins: n=25 codes {401: 25} median latency 0.052 s'; 'concurrent (20 at a time) n=40 codes {401: 40} median 0.86 s, max 1.55 s'. Code: backend/gridlytics/auth.py:52, 79-80; routes_local.py:76-99; platform.py:564-578.

title: A suspended or pending membership is told 'You are not a member of that company'
label: ux
role: member whose membership the founder suspended or left pending
steps:
1. The founder PATCHes /api/founder/users/{id}/memberships/{B} with {status: suspended}, then with {status: pending}.
2. The member calls GET /api/platform/org with X-Gridlytics-Company: B.
expected: A sentence that names the state and who can change it, e.g. 'Your membership of B is suspended; ask its owner or OnyxLeaf'. Boxlytics keeps 'suspended' and 'pending' as states of their own.
actual: Both states give 403 not_a_member, 'You are not a member of that company in Gridlytics; choose one of yours', because companies._counted drops non-active memberships before _choose. A person with only that company falls through to no_company and the not-set-up page.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f64857cc-0ca7-5cbb-b665-d2b474fb2fb8/scratchpad/audit/supa-auth/t2.out: '3 B suspended, header B: 403 ... not_a_member'; '3b B pending, header B: 403 ... not_a_member'. Code: backend/gridlytics/companies.py:231-258 (identical in Solarlytics).

2. Read THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and DESIGN_LOG lines 244-257.
expected: Plan Part 10.4 step 7 and U2 line 600: record in DESIGN_LOG's first section the founder token format's origin in Boxlytics' supabase/functions/_shared/founder-auth.ts at c429bef. actual: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES lists only solarlytics-backend@c853130. DESIGN_LOG mentions only that 'the founder password accepts Boxlytics' plain sha256 with a warning, as the lifted code did'.
